harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2, node3 (standbys) on RHEL 10, generating the replicator credential on node1 and distributing it node-to-node over SSH (never printed). Verified live replication, then exercised failover: stopped node1, promoted node2 to writable primary with zero committed-data loss, reparented node3 to stream from node2, and re-provisioned node1 as a standby of node2 via pg_basebackup. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time node-restart protocol on all three nodes (node1, node3, then primary node2 last), proving changed OS boot IDs and full PostgreSQL/replication recovery (including node2 correctly resuming as primary and both standbys auto-reattaching) after each restart, with a final end-to-end write replicated to both standbys.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 on node1, node2, node3
Initialized primary DB on node1, configured wal_level/replica settings and pg_hba.conf for replication
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes
Generated replicator role password on node1 via /dev/urandom (never printed) and created the replication role without exposing the password in output
Distributed the password to node2/node3 over cluster SSH keys, avoiding literal secrets in commands
Cloned node2 and node3 as standbys of node1 via pg_basebackup -R, created physical replication slots, started replication, verified streaming state and replicated a test table
Captured pre-failover committed data and confirmed it was present on both standbys
Simulated primary loss by stopping postgresql on node1; promoted node2 via pg_promote() with zero committed-data loss (rows 1-2 intact) and confirmed a new write succeeded
Reparented node3 to stream from node2 (updated primary_conninfo/primary_slot_name, verified streaming state)
Rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via pg_basebackup and confirmed it rejoined with full data including post-failover writes
Verified full 3-node topology (node2 primary, node1+node3 standbys) with a final committed write replicated to both standbys
Captured per-node boot_id and postgres/replication health baseline
Restarted node1, node3, then node2 (the primary, restarted last) one at a time via systemctl reboot with background-launched command so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled each node's exec availability post-restart and confirmed changed boot_id after each restart
Verified post-restart recovery: node1 and node3 rejoined as standbys with all historical data, node2 resumed correctly as primary (not standby) with both standbys auto-reattached
Performed a final end-to-end write on node2 and confirmed replication to node1 and node3 after all restarts

evidence.requirement: 3-node streaming replication established, node1 primary writable, node2/node3 standbys
evidence.summary: Postgres started on node1, node2/node3 base-backed up from node1 with -R, pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming via active physical slots, and a test row inserted on node1 replicated to both standbys with pg_is_in_recovery=true on each

evidence.requirement: Credentials generated on managed nodes, not exposed
evidence.summary: Replicator password generated via /dev/urandom directly on node1 filesystem and consumed server-side by psql variable substitution; role created without the password ever appearing in command args or output

evidence.requirement: Failover: standby takes over as writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: Committed row 'pre-failover-committed' verified present on both standbys before disruption; node1 postgres stopped; node2 promoted via pg_promote() to pg_is_in_recovery=false; post-promotion query shows rows 1 and 2 intact plus a new write, proving no data loss

evidence.requirement: Surviving standby re-parented to new primary during failover
evidence.summary: node3 primary_conninfo repointed from node1 to node2, restarted, confirmed streaming to node2 (pg_stat_replication) and pg_is_in_recovery=true with post-failover data present

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary rejoins as standby of the new primary
evidence.summary: node1 re-cloned via pg_basebackup from node2, started as standby (pg_is_in_recovery=true) with all historical and post-failover data; node2 pg_stat_replication shows both node1 and node3 streaming with active slots; a final cluster-wide write replicated to both

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6ab6a71b captured with postgres active/standby-healthy; systemctl reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to ed875a28 after reconnect; postgres active, standby recovery confirmed with all data; node2 shows node1 reattached to replication

evidence.requirement: Node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 19062a82 captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to bbd64094 after reconnect; postgres active, standby recovery confirmed with all data intact

evidence.requirement: Node2 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state as primary with quorum
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 03408ac4 captured with node2 as writable primary and 2 streaming replicas; reboot acknowledged (restarted last, after node1/node3 quorum confirmed healthy); boot_id changed to df7ca49a after reconnect; node2 resumed correctly as primary (not standby) with both standbys auto-reattached; final write replicated to both node1 and node3
